archetypes.name: env-file-dataflow
archetypes.rationale: The emit-tally preserve guard depends on OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT being correctly written by tally-code-votes.sh and parsed from review-tally.env; a missing write or format mismatch silently re-introduces the overwrite bug regardless of the guard logic.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that tally-code-votes.sh already writes OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT into the file passed as --tally-file (review-tally.env) and that emit-tally.sh's --tally-file parsing path is implemented or described. Check whether the env file uses KEY=VALUE lines and whether the plan's 'coerce non-numeric to 0' logic correctly handles an absent key without masking a missing write. If emit-tally currently reads OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT via a different mechanism (e.g., exported env var rather than file parse), the preserve guard evaluates to 0 and silently re-introduces the tally-overwrite bug even after the fix lands. Confirm that the test-emit-tally.sh cases seed the tally file in exactly the format tally-code-votes.sh produces, not a hand-crafted approximation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: seq-space-collision
archetypes.rationale: Two independent OOS_WRITE_SEQ counters — tally starting from 0, review-and-fix starting from existing accumulated-oos.md block count — can produce colliding OOS_N ids if tally-written blocks are not yet in accumulated-oos.md when review-and-fix reads its starting count.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the data flow from tally-code-votes.sh writing to oos-accepted-review.md and review-and-fix.sh writing to accumulated-oos.md: determine whether tally-written blocks are present in accumulated-oos.md before review-and-fix.sh initializes OOS_WRITE_SEQ from its block count, or whether they arrive only via copy_to_parent after review-and-fix completes. If tally blocks are absent at init time, review-and-fix starts from 0 and both producers emit OOS_1, OOS_2, etc., creating duplicate ids in the merged file. Also check that oos-non-security-block-count.awk used as the seq initializer is aware of the reader-hardening extension for legacy tagged headers, and confirm whether --seq 0 is a valid argument to normalize-oos-block-header.sh given the plan's 'non-negative integer' spec. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: normalize-awk-contract
archetypes.rationale: The normalize helper awk sub() pattern must apply only to line 1 of each block and must escape & in replacements; a bare sub() or unescaped & silently corrupts titles or rewrites wrong lines.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the proposed awk sub() pattern in normalize-oos-block-header.sh against all header forms tally-code-votes.sh can produce: bare ### FINDING_N:, tagged ### FINDING_N: [OUT_OF_SCOPE], and existing ### OOS_N:. Verify the 'line 1 only' constraint is expressed as an NR==1 guard in POSIX awk rather than relying on sub() not matching subsequent lines, since multi-line block files passed via --block-file could have a second ### header. Check that & in the replacement string is correctly handled — awk sub() treats & as the matched text, so a title containing & (e.g., 'Strunk & White') would be silently corrupted unless escaped; BASH_AUTHORING.md documents this exact hazard for renderer substitutions. Confirm that the test-normalize-oos-block-header.sh harness includes a fixture with & in the title text to guard against silent corruption. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
